title: Meteorology-driven partitioning of emerging contaminants between PM2.5 and coarse PM10–2.5 aerosols
content: Atmospheric emerging contaminants (ECs) are carried by particle fractions whose composition can change with weather. We paired PM2.5 and operationally separated coarse PM10–2.5 samples in the Guanzhong Plain, combining UHPLC-MS/MS, nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), and interpretable machine learning. Summer screening profiles suggested stronger size-dependent partitioning than winter profiles; chemical labels are candidate annotations, not independently confirmed structures. Winter showed weaker separation, consistent with a more mixed stagnation-influenced regime. Two archived extracts labelled as fine- and coarse-fraction-derived had NTA hydrodynamic modes of 139.6 and 199.0 nm; these sizes do not establish polymer identity. Temperature dominated summer associations, while winter relationships also involved precipitation and radiation. These results support weather-responsive, size-resolved monitoring of atmospheric EC mixtures. These fitted associations are exploratory: PLSR prediction was poorer than a training-mean baseline, and tree-model performance was mixed. Independent validation beyond the two short campaigns is required.
